title: Roadmap Escalation Record
description: One line of an append-only `planning/roadmaps/<roadmap>/escalations.jsonl` (scripted-liaison-sweep-design section 3). Exists because the scripted sweep that replaces the full-time liaison must be able to diff a lane-authored escalation without parsing prose: the notes.md entry required by begin-orchestration.md Rule 5 carries the reasoning for a human or a fresh agent, this record carries the same fact in a shape a script can diff. Never rewritten, never rotated -- mirrors lane-log.jsonl and drain-log.jsonl. `kind` covers begin-orchestration.md Rule 6's four 'what you still must not decide alone' cases -- an operator gate, a bailed block's fate, two blocks that genuinely disagree, and anything that would edit another lane's repo -- one `kind` value each, plus two values NOT drawn from that list: `interrupt-request` (a timing question, not an ownership one) and `finding` (a discovered fact not yet triaged). This schema deliberately requires `verified_at_sha` (NOT in the design doc's own field table) -- `verified_by` records HOW a claim was checked but carries no date, so a stale escalation is indistinguishable from a fresh one without the git SHA the record was written against; this is the exact 'carried consequences after the world moved' defect the whole initiative exists to fix.

ts_utc.description: Full ISO-8601 with a `Z` or numeric offset -- a date-only value is rejected, the same trap OKF frontmatter's `timestamp` field documents (docs/okf-frontmatter.md trap #4).

repo.description: Repo slug the escalating lane is driving, e.g. `bastion`, `engine-rs`.

lane.description: Lane name as registered in the BT.6.A lane-agent registry.

kind.description: `operator-gate`, `bail`, `disagreement`, and `cross-repo-edit` each map to one of begin-orchestration.md Rule 6's four 'what you still must not decide alone' cases. `interrupt-request` and `finding` do not come from that list. `cross-repo-edit` is an ownership question ('I need a change in territory I don't own'), not a timing question -- never map it to `interrupt-request`. It is normally resolved by pinging the owning lane and writing to its durable home (begin-orchestration.md ~line 409), not by waking the operator: the sweep routes `cross-repo-edit` to the owning lane's queue, never to a human interrupt.

block.description: The block id this escalation is scoped to, if any.

channel.description: The lane declares this at gate-definition time -- never the sweep script. `session:<slug>` for any richer channel; `notification` only for a reducible yes/no already declared as such.

gate_id.description: `<roadmap>/<repo>/<block>`, matching notify-operator's `--gate-id` scoping so a stale tap can never resolve a different lane's question.

summary.description: Mirrors the WhatsApp body-text limit (core/engine-rs/crates/engine-core/src/operator/limits.rs:20, the `WHATSAPP_MAX_BODY_CHARS` const at line 55) so a `notification`-channel escalation is composable without truncation.

verified_by.description: Same contract as ping-agent's field: either a literal command and its real output (a command line, then its output on a following line), or `UNVERIFIED: <who claimed it>`. A bare adjective such as `measured` satisfies neither shape.

verified_at_sha.description: The short git SHA at write time OF THE SUBJECT REPO -- the repo the `verified_by` command actually ran in, NOT the brain root. A claim whose command cds into a sub-repo is dated by that sub-repo's HEAD; the brain SHA says nothing about whether the checked thing moved, so comparing against it flags every cross-repo escalation permanently stale. Dates the `verified_by` claim so a stale escalation is distinguishable from a fresh one. Not in the design doc's own field table; added because `verified_by` alone carries no date.

durable_home.description: Where the prose twin of this record lives, e.g. `{"channel":"run-record","ref":"<repo>/planning/orchestration-run/<roadmap>/notes.md#<anchor>"}` -- this record supplements that write, it never replaces it.

clears_when.description: A predicate describing when this escalation is resolved. Never author one already satisfied -- the same rule as state.json carryover[].

options.description: The operator's response options for a `channel: notification` escalation, declared by the lane at gate-definition time -- never composed by the sweep script (scripted-liaison-sweep-design section 5: 'the script decides whether to wake an agent; it never decides the answer'). Required when `channel` is `notification`; forbidden otherwise, since a `session:<slug>` channel is never reduced to buttons (Invariant 2, core/engine-rs/crates/engine-core/src/operator/channel.rs:4: 'declared at gate-definition time, never degraded'). Enforces the real `bastion notify ask` CLI limits: 2 to 3 options (OPERATOR_MIN_RESPONSE_OPTIONS=2, WHATSAPP_MAX_REPLY_BUTTONS=3, core/engine-rs/crates/engine-core/src/operator/limits.rs:47,40 -- a single option is rejected the same as zero, since a 'decision, never a task' payload must offer a real choice), each label at most 20 chars (WHATSAPP_MAX_BUTTON_LABEL_CHARS, limits.rs:51).

key.description: The machine-readable value returned when the operator picks this option.

label.description: The button text shown to the operator -- capped at 20 chars, the WhatsApp reply-button title limit (limits.rs:49).
